items.title: Winners And Losers Of Q2: Amgen (NASDAQ:AMGN) Vs The Rest Of The Therapeutics Stocks
items.summary: As the craze of earnings season draws to a close, here’s a look back at some of the most exciting (and some less so) results from Q2. Today, we are looking at therapeutics stocks, starting with Amgen (NASDAQ:AMGN).

items.title: Can Eli Lilly Stock Catch Up To Rivals It Outgrows?
items.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) grew revenue 49.6% over the last twelve months, the fastest of the six companies in its peer group. It also runs the group's widest operating margin, at 49.7%. Yet its 53.4% stock return ranks only third, behind Merck and Johnson & Johnson, which both grew far more slowly. The open question is how long Mounjaro and Zepbound can carry a lead the stock has not matched.

items.title: How a Roth IRA Can Keep Thousands More of Your DJIA Dividend Income Compounding
items.summary: Holding blue-chip Dow dividend payers in a taxable account quietly hands the IRS a cut of every reinvested dollar, year after year, and the compounding cost over two decades is far steeper than most investors expect.

items.title: Amgen (AMGN) Is Up 7.9% After Positive Phase 3 Dazodalibep Data in Systemic Sjögren’s Disease

items.title: Viking's Obesity Edge May Be Staying Power, Not Weight Loss
items.summary: Viking Therapeutics shares jumped 36% after VK2735 maintenance data showed patients kept most weight loss on less frequent dosing, though Phase 3 results and commercial funding remain unresolved.

items.title: AMGN's Dazodalibep Meets Goal in Systemic Sjogren's Disease Study
items.summary: Amgen's dazodalibep meets its primary goal in a Phase III study, showing sustained improvement in systemic Sjogren's disease activity through week 48.
